question: Cobalt is present in which vitamin?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin B12**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cobalt is a major component of vitamin B12, also known as cobalamin: 
 
• Vitamin B12 is a large, complex molecule that's not found in plants.
 
• However, if a diet contains enough cobalt, intestinal and ruminal bacteria can synthesize vitamin B12.
 
• Adults need about 1.5 micrograms of vitamin B12 per day. 
 
• Vitamin B12 is an important micronutrient for many eukaryotic phytoplankton in the marine environment.
 
• It's also found in very small quantities in seawater. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vitamin B1, B3, and B5 are all B vitamins, which are a group of water-soluble vitamins that play important roles in the body's cellular function: 
 
• Vitamin B1 (thiamin): Also known as vitamin F, this vitamin is a sulfur-containing member of the B complex family. 
 
• Vitamin B3 (niacin): Helps the body release energy from food and keeps the nervous system and skin healthy. 
 
• Vitamin B5 (pantothenic acid): One of the eight B vitamins that make up the B complex. 
 
• Here are some other B vitamins:
 
• Vitamin B2 (riboflavin): Involved in oxidation and reduction reactions 
 
• Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine): Can cause anemia, depression, dermatitis, confusion, skin rashes, and infection if deficient 
 
• Vitamin B7 (biotin): Part of the B complex 
 
• Vitamin B9 (folate): Works with vitamin B12 to synthesize nucleic acid
